subject: MedPay retention carveout: structured logs + conditional TTL discussion
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ong <sarah.ong@medpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: data handling constraints & proposed conditional TTL approach

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a concrete proposal to move the compliance conversation forward.

What I heard from MedPay:
- Primary constraint: no raw PHI persistence in Redwood-hosted storage beyond a very short window.
- Desired outcome: either a 0-retention model for sensitive fields or an auditable short TTL (hours) with strong encryption & access controls.
- Legal/security want explicit guarantees around logging (what is retained, for how long) and a dataflow diagram showing where tokens/keys/unencrypted data transit.

Redwood proposal (high level):
- Structured logs model: we persist only structured metadata (request timestamps, model id, request size, routing metadata) and we redact or hash sensitive fields (PII/PHI) before any log storage.
- Conditional TTL option: raw request payload encrypted in transit, kept in ephemeral storage for up to 48 hours (configurable); KV cache entries (for latency) can be scoped to 0–24 hours depending on workload; optional automatic purge hooks.
- Alternative for the strictest requirement: private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where MedPay controls long-term storage and keys — enables true 0-retention on Redwood-managed runtime.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short proposal (redwood-conditional-ttl-proposal.pdf) that outlines the technical controls, encryption/KMS model, and a few operational safeguards (audit logs, access revocation workflows).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Can you confirm whether MedPay’s minimum acceptable TTL for non-redacted payloads is 0 hours, 2 hours, or up to 24 hours? This will guide which path (hosted conditional TTL vs private deployment) is most appropriate.
2) Per your request, I’ll send a simple dataflow diagram showing where tokens and unredacted data exist transiently. (Attaching a stub image next).
3) If legal wants, I can loop in Kimberly from Redwood Legal to draft language for a carveout/BAA that clarifies retention and auditability.

If helpful, we’re available for a 30–45m security deep-dive next week with your security and legal teams.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0149
https://redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-conditional-ttl-proposal.pdf (summary, 3 pages)
From: Sarah Ong <sarah.ong@medpay.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: MedPay Legal <legal@medpay.com>, MedPay Security <security@medpay.com>, Alex Liu <alex.liu@medpay.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: data handling constraints & proposed conditional TTL approach

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Short answer on TTL preference: MedPay’s security posture prefers 0 retention for any PHI-containing payloads in vendor-managed systems. We can accept short-lived transient storage for processing (e.g., tokenization) but it should not persist beyond processing+verification.
- For non-PHI telemetry/structured logs (latency, model id, error codes), we’re OK with longer retention if PII is never present in those logs.
- Our Security team wants a dataflow diagram and confirmation that any hashed values cannot be reversed and that KMS keys are customer-controlled or rotated per our schedule.

We’ve attached a simple dataflow image (medpay-dataflow-stub.png) that highlights our expected boundaries — please review and confirm where Redwood would store/transform data.

Can your team confirm whether the hosted conditional TTL can be configured to a strict 0h persistence for fields flagged as PHI and still provide the performance SLAs we need? If not, we’ll need to explore Private deployment options.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex from Security will coordinate a 1-hour deep dive if you can share an updated architecture note beforehand.

Best,
Sarah Ong
Head of Product Security | MedPay Solutions
sarah.ong@medpay.com

Attachment: medpay-dataflow-stub.png (image, 1MB stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ong <sarah.ong@medpay.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 20:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: data handling constraints & proposed conditional TTL approach

Hi all —

Looping in legal here with a couple pragmatic options that keep the deal moving while protecting MedPay’s requirements. High-level thoughts:

Option A — Hosted conditional TTL (fastest path):
- Redwood implements field-level redaction/hashing for any PHI markers before logs are written.
- Customer-managed KMS with envelope encryption for any short-lived storage.
- Contract language: confirm maximum retention window (we recommend 48 hours as a reasonable ops buffer) and include audit rights + kill-switch for forensic purge.

Option B — Private deployment pilot (strongest guarantee):
- Deploy Redwood Private in MedPay VPC or on-prem. Keys never leave customer boundary; Redwood only receives telemetry necessary for support. This enables true 0-retention on vendor-managed surfaces.

Operational asks from our side:
- We will need a sample PoC run to validate latency impact if you require 0 retention on PHI fields. Some workloads will need a short KV cache (seconds–minutes) to meet SLOs and we should quantify that.
- Legal draft attached (legal-ttl-draft.docx) with suggested carveout language and a short definition of what we treat as "raw payload" vs "structured telemetry."

If MedPay needs a hard 0h guarantee for all raw payloads in hosted mode, we should prepare the private deployment path concurrently — that will be the lowest-risk option for both sides.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap: data handling constraints & proposed conditional TTL approach

Sarah / Alex —

Thanks for the quick feedback. We’ll do the following:
1) Security deep-dive: proposing Tue 2026-09-29 10:00am PT — 1 hour with your security team. Please confirm availability.
2) Updated proposal: Kimberly and Neha will incorporate MedPay feedback into the conditional TTL doc and mark explicit fields as "non-persistent in hosted mode". I’ll circulate the updated redwood-conditional-ttl-proposal.pdf before the call.
3) Pilot options: if MedPay confirms the requirement for absolute 0 retention on PHI, we’ll prioritize a Private deployment pilot timeline and provide a cost/ops delta in the next 3 business days.

Please reply with the preferred time for the deep-dive and the best contact for scheduling (Alex?).

Cheers,
Mateo
